steps.versicle: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.
steps.title: Sign of the Cross

steps.versicle: O Jesus, meek and humble of heart.

invocations: From the desire of being esteemed,
From the desire of being loved,
From the desire of being extolled,
From the desire of being honored,
From the desire of being praised,
From the desire of being preferred to others,
From the desire of being consulted,
From the desire of being approved,
From the fear of being humiliated,
From the fear of being despised,
From the fear of suffering rebukes,
From the fear of being calumniated,
From the fear of being forgotten,
From the fear of being ridiculed,
From the fear of being wronged,
From the fear of being suspected,
steps.title: Deliverances (each answered: Deliver me, Jesus.)

invocations: That others may be loved more than I,
That others may be esteemed more than I,
That, in the opinion of the world, others may increase and I may decrease,
That others may be chosen and I set aside,
That others may be praised and I unnoticed,
That others may be preferred to me in everything,
That others may become holier than I, provided that I may become as holy as I should,
steps.response: Jesus, grant me the grace to desire it.
steps.title: Petitions (each answered: Jesus, grant me the grace to desire it.)

schedule_note.note: The Litany of Humility in its received devotional text, traditionally attributed to Cardinal Rafael Merry del Val (d. 1930); the prayer circulated in equivalent forms from the 1870s-1880s and the received wording is public domain. Two litany steps, both rendered as individual call and response: the sixteen deliverances answered "Deliver me, Jesus." and the seven petitions answered "Jesus, grant me the grace to desire it." The session’s opening versicles are received formulas; the pack needs no content entries — the litany text is the session.
schedule_note.invocation_source: Litany of Humility (traditionally attributed to Cardinal Merry del Val, 1865-1930)
